candidateOutput.title: Trapping Rain Water
candidateOutput.crux: Calculate total trapped water between bars based on max left/right heights for each position.
edgeCases: all zeros: water never trapped, return 0
two peaks with large valley: water fills valley up to min height
height[i]=10^5 extremes: large values but bounded sum
height length=2*10^4: need O(n) not O(n^2)
duplicates: plateaus stop water flow if not lower than neighbors
max at one end: no right/left bound for interior bars

wrongApproaches.name: Naive left/right max scanning per index
wrongApproaches.signal: Two loops over array computing maxLeft[i] and maxRight[i] for each i
wrongApproaches.reason: O(N) space + O(N) time per index yields O(N^2) total.

wrongApproaches.name: Two pointers without maintaining maxes
wrongApproaches.signal: Two moving pointers comparing current heights only
wrongApproaches.reason: Misses cases where a lower bar is bounded by higher but non-adjacent walls.

wrongApproaches.name: Stack simulation only for peak valleys
wrongApproaches.signal: Using stack to track monotonic heights per index
wrongApproaches.reason: Stack approach also ends up O(N) per index in worst case.

optimal.name: Two Pointers with Left/Right Max Tracking
optimal.keyIdea: Traverse with left and right pointers, tracking max heights seen from each side; water at lower side uses its own max to compute depth.
invariants: while (left < right) compare height[left] and height[right]
update water using the smaller max side
pitfalls: Initialize leftMax/rightMax = 0, but need actual heights at boundaries
Off-by-one: do not add water when height equals current max (no trap)
Pointer update must move the lower side to continue capturing water beyond
Overflow: accumulate water in long to avoid int sum overflow
recognizeBy: if (height[left] < height[right]) { leftMax = Math.max(leftMax, height[left]); water += leftMax - height[left]; left++; } else { ... }

alternates.name: Prefix Max + Suffix Max Arrays
alternates.keyIdea: Precompute leftMax array and rightMax array then sum min(leftMax[i], rightMax[i]) - height[i] for each i.
alternates.whyNotOptimal: O(N) extra memory and two passes may exceed limits for n=2*10^4 and space constraints.

alternates.name: Brute Force per Index
alternates.keyIdea: For each index, scan left for max and right for max, accumulate water = min(leftMax, rightMax) - height[i].
alternates.whyNotOptimal: Quadratic time fails for n up to 2*10^4.

alternates.name: Dynamic Programming on valleys
alternates.keyIdea: DP[i] stores water trapped at i; use DP[i] = max(0, min(leftMax, rightMax) - height[i]).
alternates.whyNotOptimal: Extra DP array and repeated min/max calculations add overhead but still O(N).
recognizeBy: for (i) dp[i] = Math.max(0, Math.min(leftMax[i], rightMax[i]) - height[i]);

alternates.name: Monotonic Stack with area calculation
alternates.keyIdea: Use stack to store indices of increasing heights; when a higher bar is encountered, pop and compute trapped water using stack top and current bar.
alternates.whyNotOptimal: Stack operations add constant overhead and extra memory, still linear but slower in practice.
recognizeBy: int curr = height[i]; while (!stack.isEmpty() && height[stack.peek()] < curr) ...
